dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: na dveṣam bhāvayet kvāpi na rāgam bhāvayet kvacit | rāgadveṣavinirmuktau madhye brahma prasarpati ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one cultivate aversion nowhere and attachment nowhere; when one is free of both attachment and aversion, brahman spreads forth in the middle.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: equality of consciousness (samatā) is the point of both verses 125 and 126; in 125 it comes from contemplating brahman's presence everywhere, in 126 from rejecting both aversion and attachment. Wallis: 'neither hatred nor craving'; the absolute unfolds in the centre.
dharana.instruction: Notice each like and dislike, feed neither, and rest in the open middle between them.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 101' = verse 126 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 126 = 'Neither hatred nor craving (Y101 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 126 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 126: Neither hatred nor craving (Y101 ~ B3)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 126 'Dharana 103', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 101. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 126 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is two pulls, toward and away, and the open middle that appears when neither is fed.
geometry.svg_hint: two arrows pointing in opposite directions with an open, glowing space between them
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Feed neither
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: neither the pull toward nor the push away is fed, and something open spreads in the middle. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Notice liking and disliking, and feed neither
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Moments of liking and disliking, not fed

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one cultivate aversion nowhere and attachment nowhere; when one is free of both attachment and aversion, brahman spreads forth in the middle.
adiyogi.method_summary: As you go through the day, or sit quietly, notice each pull toward something you like and each push away from something you dislike. Do not feed either one. Rest in the open middle that appears between them.

honesty.disclosure: Door 101 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 101 (verse 126) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 101 is dharana 101, verse 126. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This is not suppressing feelings or ignoring danger; it is simply not feeding the pull or the push. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 101: neither aversion nor attachment. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 101, verse 126.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit, or carry this into the day. The map is two pulls, toward and away, and the open middle.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Notice a pull toward something. Notice a push away from something. Feed neither. Rest in the middle that opens.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: an open space between two pulls. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 126: cultivate aversion nowhere and attachment nowhere; free of both, brahman spreads forth in the middle.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Take a slow, free breath. Carry the open middle into the next like or dislike that comes.
